historical_references.reference: The name 'Moorthy' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Murti', which means 'image' or 'form'. In Hinduism, a Murti is a physical representation of a deity, often in the form of a statue or idol. Moorthys are revered and worshipped as a manifestation of the divine being.

Another reference to the name 'Moorthy' can be found in the Tamil Sangam literature, specifically in the 'Agam' or 'Agnakkazhjar' (literally 'The Eight Poets') collection. In this context, 'Moorthy' refers to a poet and scholar, who was one of the revered sages of the Sangam age. The exact time period of the Sangam age is debated, but it is generally believed to have occurred between the 2nd century BCE and the 4th century CE.
